name: – Niclas Herbst – After § 16 – Am 66
title: REPORT on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the European Union for the financial year 2023, Section III – Commission, executive agencies and the ninth, tenth and eleventh European Development Funds
part_text: 16 a. Deplores, however, the reality of the European Commission's complacency towards Islamist movements and entities; witnesses the European Commission's funding of nearly 10 million euros for the so-called “European Koran” project to rewrite European history, the “EU Action Plan against Racism 2020-2025” and its follow-up, which targets all forms of racism with the exception of anti-white racism, or the funding of Erasmus + or NGOs in Europe (Femyso close to the Muslim Brotherhood, Islamic Relief Worldwide, etc., as well as extra-European universities close to the Muslim Brotherhood, as well as non-European universities close to Islamist movements (Gaza University, close to Hamas); thus demonstrates that the European Commission knowingly contributes to inciting, by financing them, non-European interference in the territory of Member States, with principles that run counter to European values; regrets that the European Commission does not verify the final beneficiaries of its funding, some of whom are close to terrorist or Islamist movements, thus contributing to their direct or indirect support from European funds; condemns these practices and urges the European Commission to put an end to them and initiate procedures to recover these undue funds; regrets the absence of a consensual definition of the rule of law as a fundamental value of the Union, and the biased use of it arbitrarily made by the Commission;
